title: kx-plot: one-line matplotlib plots
subtitle: One-line matplotlib plots and themes for Kaggle notebooks
description:
**kx**: one-line matplotlib plots and themes for Kaggle notebooks. Plain Python, works offline, so it also runs in competition notebooks with no internet.

## Setup
Attach this dataset (**Add Input → Datasets → kx-plot**), then:
```python
import sys; sys.path.append('/kaggle/input/datasets/vhrabar/kx-plot')
import kx; kx.use('dark')
```

## One-liner plots
```python
kx.plot(x, y, z, 'scatter-grid-leg')            # spec: kind-theme-flag-...
kx.plot(df, 'month', 'y2025', 'y2026', 'bar')   # DataFrame columns by name
kx.plot(df, 'value', spec='kde', by='group')    # one curve per group
kx.plot(x, y, 'line-paper', linewidth=3)        # theme for this plot; other keywords go to matplotlib
```

| token | values |
|---|---|
| kind | `line` `step` `area` `band` `scatter` `bar` `barh` `hist` `kde` `ridge` `ecdf` `box` `violin` `strip` `qq` |
| theme | `dark` `light` `paper` `science` `talk` `poster` `thesis` |
| flags, every kind | `grid` `leg` `legout` `tight` `rot` `logx` `logy` `logxy` `symlogy` `zero` `eq` `pct` `si` |
| flags, some kinds | `stack` `norm` `cum` `date` `mk` `sort` `ann` `mean` `median` `nocb` `sym` `logc` |

Unknown tokens raise an error with the closest valid ones as a hint. `kx.grammar()` lists everything, `kx.grammar('ridge')` explains one kind, and `kx.parse(spec)` shows how a spec is read.

## Themes, layouts, saving
```python
kx.use('light', palette='okabe', cmap='batlow')   # notebook default
with kx.context('science'):                        # just this block
    for ax, col in zip(kx.grid(3), df.columns):    # 3 panels as a flat array of axes
        kx.plot(df, col, spec='hist', ax=ax)
    kx.save('figure.png')                          # lands in /kaggle/working
```
Palettes include Okabe-Ito, Paul Tol, Petroff, Tableau and ColorBrewer; colourmaps include cmocean and Crameri (vendored). `kx.palettes()` and `kx.cmaps()` list them.

## Contents
- `kx/`: the package (`import kx`): themes in `kx/styles/`, demo data for `kx.load()` in `kx/data/` (`kx.datasets()` lists it)
- `previews/`: one PNG per theme showing every kind, and a demo notebook

Nothing is hidden: `kx.show('dark')` prints a theme, `kx.source('scatter')` the code that draws a kind.

Source, full walkthrough and issues: https://github.com/vhrabar/kx-plot
